## SQL performance M0 — inventory, baseline and ranked list (#33633)

Measured 2026-11-15T05:06Z on `origin/main` @ `4c32b969` (line references below are on that tree). Harness: draft PR #33662 — `packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf/` (`bench.mjs` = HTTP baseline, `micro.mjs` = today-vs-target SQL pairs, README). Databases: SQLite through the `better-sqlite3` SqlDriver, PostgreSQL 16 (local cluster, `fsync=off` for loading only). Fixture: `bench_region` 20 -> `bench_account` scale/100 (**private** OWD) -> `bench_opportunity` scale/10 (`controlled_by_parent`) -> `bench_line_item` = scale (`controlled_by_parent`, lookup `bench_product` 200). The member owns every 10th account. Iterations 20 (100k) / 10 (1M), warmup 3, shared 4-core box: **statement counts are exact, milliseconds are indicative.**

**The maintainer picks what M2 files.** Nothing here was filed; one reproducible defect (R2) is flagged for the seat to file.

### Ranked list

| # | item | measured cost (today) | expected gain (target, measured by `micro.mjs` at 1M unless noted) | area | size |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| R1 | Per-measure aggregation `filter` forces the in-memory aggregate: every row of the scoped set is fetched into the app (`engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts:1341`, `:1392`) | `aggregate_measure_filter` p50: SQLite 383 ms (100k) / **6.2 s** (1M); PG 768 ms / **7.3 s** | conditional aggregate (`sum(case when … end)` / PG `FILTER (WHERE …)`) in the GROUP BY: SQLite 5.10 s -> 0.53 s, PG 5.09 s -> 0.14 s (**10x–36x**) | A4 (engine + driver-sql capability flag); A3 consumer (analytics measures) | M |
| R2 | Analytics dimension through a lookup is an FK-expand: GROUP BY the FK, then `id IN (every distinct FK value)`, then re-bucket in the app (`objectql-strategy.ts:1765`, `:1723`) | **500 DATABASE_ERROR at 1M on both dialects** (100k distinct FKs: SQLite "too many SQL variables"; PG bind count wraps to 34464); 123–131 ms at 100k | one `JOIN … GROUP BY parent.attr`: PG 182 ms -> 131 ms for the first read alone, and it stops failing. SQLite join measured slower (130 -> 363 ms vs the first read only) but the today path does not answer at all | A3 (service-analytics) | M |
| R3 | Default list order `created_at desc` has no index (system column; not in the implicit set, `schema-drift.ts:2295`) — every default-ordered page sorts its whole filtered set | unfiltered admin list p50: SQLite 1.31 s, PG 326 ms at 1M | index `(created_at, id)`: unfiltered page SQLite 1237 ms -> **0.09 ms**, PG 69 ms -> 0.38 ms; member page PG 110 ms -> 3.1 ms (SQLite's planner keeps the chain-first plan: 146 -> 154 ms) | A4 (schema sync implicit indexes) — needs a ruling: the implicit-index ruling excluded system columns for want of a measured read | S |
| R4 | Unrestricted (admin) reads of a `controlled_by_parent` detail still carry the composed chain `fk IN (SELECT id FROM master WHERE fk2 IN (SELECT id FROM master2))` (`engine-readable-ids-permission-formula.ts:207` composes `ReadableIds.compose(leaf, undefined)`; leaf from `security-plugin-cbp-read-filter.ts:156`); the analytics path ANDs the same chain twice | rides on every admin list, count and aggregate above (`list_filter_sort` admin 630 ms SQLite / 238 ms PG at 1M) | drop the vacuous leaf: page SQLite 397 -> 281 ms, PG 97 -> 56 ms; total SQLite 217 -> 136 ms, PG 78 -> 54 ms (**−29% to −42%**, twice per list). Caveat for the decision: the chain also hides orphan details (no master row) | A2 (plugin-security leaf) + A4 (engine composition) | S–M, needs decision (orphan semantics) |
| R5 | Cross-object filter (`{ opportunity: { stage: 'won' } }`) reads the related ids as the caller, then `$in` (`engine-query-lowering.ts:184-217`, `RELATION_FILTER_ID_CAP = 1000`); the id read runs twice per list (page + total) | **400 INVALID_FILTER already at 100k** (20k matching opportunities > 1000); small match (`product.family`) p50 PG 328 ms / SQLite 991 ms at 1M | a nested subquery leaf, composed like ReadableIds so the related object's read scope still applies: the refused query is served in PG 198 ms / SQLite 376 ms; small match PG 153 -> 122 ms, SQLite 627 -> 615 ms | A4 (objectql lowering + driver compile) | M |
| R6 | Non-UTC date bucket forces the in-memory aggregate (ADR-0053 Phase 2 D2, UTC-only native bucketing; `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts:1323-1341`) | `analytics_month_tz` p50 at 1M (100k opportunities): PG 694 ms, SQLite 379 ms | zone-aware SQL bucket: PG 429 -> 40 ms (**11x**), SQLite 198 -> 71 ms (fixed-offset only — SQLite has no tz database, so DST zones stay in memory there) | A4 — amends ADR-0053 D2 for PG (new ADR status line) | M, needs decision |
| R7 | Cascade delete is one full engine `delete`/`update` per dependent (`engine-cascade-planning.ts:1085-1171`), each with its hooks, recycle-bin capture and probes | **155 statements** to delete one opportunity with 10 line items (~15 per child), p50 121–237 ms; linear in children | per relation: one id read + one `DELETE … WHERE fk = ?` (or `UPDATE … SET fk = NULL`) + one batched recycle-bin capture when the child has no per-row hooks; not measured as SQL (needs the batched capture shape first) | A4 (engine) + A3 (trash / recycle bin) | M–L |
| R8 | Per-request identity and permission resolution: a plain list is 10 statements, 2 of them data; cold it is ~21 (`sys_session` x2, `sys_user` x3–5, `sys_member` x4 incl. the organization's member list up to 1000 rows a page `resolve-authz-context.ts:2406`, permission sets x2, positions x2, metadata activation x2). The grants cache exists and is OFF by default (`OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS=0`) | fixed 7–8 statements per request admin, 11–12 member, 29 on a member's record page (`record_page` member 31 vs 18 admin) | on a local database these are ~1–3 ms; on a network database each is a round trip (Turso, managed PG). Not measured over a network | A1 (session) + A2 (security) + core authz | M |
| R9 | Sharing read scope materializes `sys_record_share.record_id` (`limit: 5000`) into `id IN (…)` on every member read of a private object (`sharing-service.ts:747-764`); hierarchy scopes expand owner ids in the app (`:742`) | **unmeasured**: the fixture holds no shares and no hierarchy (needs a share-seeding leg) | `id IN (SELECT record_id FROM sys_record_share WHERE …)`; also removes the 5000-grant ceiling (read-only inference: grants past 5000 look silently dropped, fail-closed — not reproduced, not filed) | A2 (plugin-sharing) | S–M |
| R10 | Roll-up summary recompute: per distinct parent per summary field, one aggregate + one full engine `update` on every child write (`engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts:458-470`) | **unmeasured** (fixture has no summary fields) | one grouped aggregate `… WHERE fk IN (…) GROUP BY fk` per descriptor + batched parent updates | A4 | M |
| R11 | `owner_id` (the column a private-OWD read filters on) has no index — system column, excluded by the same ruling as R3 | small at 10k accounts: account list SQLite 1.6 -> 1.4 ms, PG 1.5 -> 1.3 ms; chain count unchanged | grows with private-object size; rides with R3's ruling | A4 | S |
| R12 | Every paged list also runs `count(*)` with the full predicate (`protocol-data-crud.ts:803`; `$count=false` opts out) | member read-scoped total: PG 35 ms vs the page's 118 ms today | becomes the dominant cost once R3 lands (page 3 ms, total 35 ms); a Console that does not need `total` can send `$count=false` today | E1 (list door) + UI | S |

Not ranked (one extra statement, already batched): `$expand` reads `id IN (…)` per expanded field per page (`engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts:593`); master-detail header reads (`engine-referential-integrity.ts:514`). Turso remote advertises no date granularity, so every bucket there is in memory (`driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts:887`) — not measured, no Turso here.

### Inventory (by the card's five categories)

| category | site (@4c32b969) | trigger | SQL shape it should become |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| id list, then `$in` | `objectql/src/engine-query-lowering.ts:184-217` | nested relation condition in any `where` (find, count, aggregate) | correlated / nested subquery leaf (R5) |
| id list, then `$in` | `plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts:742-764` | every member read of a private-OWD object | `id IN (SELECT record_id FROM sys_record_share …)`; hierarchy owner set as a subquery (R9) |
| id list, then `$in` | `service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts:1765` (`resolveFkAttr`) | analytics dimension through a lookup | `JOIN` (R2) |
| id list, then `$in` | `core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:2406` | every request with an active organization (org member ids for `sys_user` scoping) | membership subquery at the `sys_user` read (R8) |
| id list, then `$in` | `objectql/src/engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts:593` | `$expand` / related-list `expand` | `LEFT JOIN` (not ranked) |
| in-memory aggregate | `objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts:1341`, `:1392` | `aggregations[].filter`; non-UTC tz + date bucket; a granularity the driver does not advertise | `FILTER (WHERE …)` / `CASE WHEN`; zone-aware bucket (R1, R6) |
| in-memory aggregate | `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts:1349` (`applyHaving`) | any `having` | `HAVING` (small: runs on aggregated rows) |
| in-memory join / regroup | `objectql-strategy.ts:1723` (`rebucketCrossObject`) | analytics cross-object dimension | `JOIN … GROUP BY` (R2) |
| N+1 | `objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts:1085-1171` | delete with `deleteBehavior: cascade` / `set_null` children | per-relation set statements (R7) |
| N+1 | `objectql/src/engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts:458-470` | any child write under a roll-up summary | grouped aggregate + batched update (R10) |
| N+1 | `objectql/src/recycle-bin/restore.ts:687-702` | restore that re-links cleared references | one `UPDATE … WHERE id IN` per field |
| N+1 | `objectql/src/assignment-rules.ts:637-639` | load-balanced assignment rule | one `GROUP BY owner_id` count |
| N+1 | `objectql/src/engine-validate.ts:408-418` | batch validate / preview (2 reads per submitted row) | one `id IN (…)` read |
| N+1 (per request) | `resolve-authz-context.ts:2402-2408`, `plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-password-session-policy.ts:183` | every authenticated request | memoised / cached identity (R8) |
| read scope in app | `sharing-service.ts:674-765` (see above) | member reads of private objects | SQL predicate (R9) |
| read scope (SQL, but vacuous) | `engine-readable-ids-permission-formula.ts:207`; `plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-read-filter.ts:156` | unrestricted reads of CBP details | omit the leaf (R4) |
| index | `driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts:2286-2310` | schema sync | **authored single-valued `lookup` / `master_detail` / `user` columns DO get `idx_TABLE_COLUMN` on both dialects (measured in the index listing); multi-valued (JSON) ones cannot** |
| index gap | `schema-drift.ts:2295` (`SYSTEM_COLUMN_NAMES`) | schema sync | `created_at` (default order), `owner_id` (private OWD) carry none (R3, R11); in single tenancy `organization_id` carried none on the fixture tables either |

### Flagged for the seat to file (class a, reproduced)

- **R2 — `POST /analytics/query` with a dimension through a lookup answers 500 `DATABASE_ERROR` once the base set holds more distinct FK values than the dialect's bind limit.** Reach: public door, measured on both dialects: cube `bench_line_item`, `dimensions: ['opportunity.stage']`, 100k distinct opportunities -> SQLite `too many SQL variables`, PostgreSQL `bind message has 34464 parameter formats but 0 parameters` (100,000 mod 65,536). ## Correction to the M0 ranked list (R3, R1, R5, R12) — #33633

Corrects the ranked-list comment 6889544281 (posted 2026-11-15T05:06Z); that comment is left as it was. Raised by review#2 on #33662. Measured 2026-11-15T05:47Z.

**What was wrong.** `micro.mjs` I8b timed the R3 index on `select * from bench_line_item order by created_at desc, id desc limit 50`. The engine does not run that statement. The admin default page it emits today still carries the vacuous controlled-by-parent chain (R4). Re-captured at 1M through `X-OS-Debug-Timing: json` on both dialects: `select * from bench_line_item where opportunity in (select id from bench_opportunity where account in (select id from bench_account)) order by created_at desc, id desc limit ?`. So the old SQLite figure "1237 ms -> 0.09 ms" was what R3 and R4 buy **together**.

**Re-measured.** `micro.mjs` as committed in `d00725a6` on #33662. Engine tree `fbccdf3f`, the stamp in the output. 1M line items, median of 7, a shared 4-core box. PostgreSQL 16 ran on a private cluster, now stopped and removed. I8b is now the chained statement; I8c is the unchained one, labelled "with R4". Each reading records the planner's plan before and after the temporary `(created_at, id)` index.

| row | SQLite run 1 | SQLite run 2 | PG |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| I8b admin page, chained (today) | 1736 -> 1328 ms | 1320 -> 1391 ms | **229 -> 0.90 ms** |
| I8c admin page, with R4 | 1707 -> 0.09 ms | 1183 -> 0.08 ms | 62 -> 0.51 ms |
| I8 member page | 163 -> 179 ms | 147 -> 145 ms | **101 -> 3.2 ms** |

Plans:
- SQLite, chained: identical before and after, in both runs: `SEARCH bench_line_item USING INDEX idx_bench_line_item_opportunity (opportunity=?) … USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY`. The index is never used. The spread between the two runs is the shared box, not the index.
- SQLite, with R4: `SCAN bench_line_item USING INDEX tmp_bench_line_item_created`.
- PG, chained, after the index: `Index Scan Backward using tmp_bench_line_item_created`, with a nested-loop semi join over the two primary keys. Before the index: parallel hash semi join, then sort.

**Does R3's gain depend on R4? On SQLite yes, on PostgreSQL no.**

Corrected R3 expected-gain cell:

> index `(created_at, id)` at 1M. **PG, independent of R4:** admin default page as emitted today (chained) 229 -> 0.9 ms; member page 101 -> 3.2 ms; with R4 as well, 62 -> 0.5 ms. **SQLite, depends on R4:** the chained page keeps its chain-first plan, identical before and after the index: 1736 -> 1328 / 1320 -> 1391 ms over two runs; member page 163 -> 179 / 147 -> 145 ms. Only with the chain dropped (R4) does the page go 1707 -> 0.09 / 1183 -> 0.08 ms. The earlier "SQLite 1237 ms -> 0.09 ms" was R3 + R4 together.

What this changes for M2:
- On PostgreSQL, R3 can be filed and land on its own.
- On SQLite, R3 alone buys nothing for these pages. Its gain arrives with R4, and R4 carries the orphan-semantics decision. File R3 with R4, or after it, if SQLite deployments are meant to benefit.
- R12's "becomes the dominant cost once R3 lands" holds on PG. On SQLite it holds once R3 and R4 land.

**R1, which SQL shape produced the 0.14 s.** It was `sum(case when … end)`: `micro.mjs` I4 times that spelling on both dialects. PG now also times `FILTER (WHERE …)` (new row I4b), and the two match.

Corrected R1 target cell:

> conditional aggregate in the GROUP BY, timed as `sum(case when quantity >= 10 then quantity end)` on both dialects. SQLite 5.13 s -> 0.54 s / 4.83 s -> 0.55 s (two runs); PG 4.39 s -> 0.144 s. PG `FILTER (WHERE quantity >= 10)` measures 0.145 s, the same within noise, so either spelling serves on PG. SQLite was not timed with `FILTER`. Earlier run: SQLite 5.10 -> 0.53 s, PG 5.09 -> 0.14 s. About 9x on SQLite and 30x–36x on PG.

**R5, the figure.** At 100k the fixture holds 10,000 opportunities, so about **2,000** are `won` (the scenario's own note says ~2000). 20k is the 1M figure. Corrected R5 cost cell: "**400 INVALID_FILTER already at 100k** (~2,000 matching opportunities, past the 1000-id cap; ~20,000 at 1M)". The 400 verdict stands.

The other rows of the 1M re-run agree with the original list within the box's run-to-run spread, and no other ranking changes. The full 1M tables for both dialects, each stamped with its commit and time, are in the follow-up comment on #33662.
